key_insight: The EHR-integrated GenAI tool detected VTE risk more sensitively than both checklist-based and clinician-judgement order set workflows, though with lower specificity.
clinical_relevance: This suggests GenAI could help identify more patients who need risk-appropriate thromboprophylaxis in inpatient care, while still requiring clinician oversight to manage false positives and missed context.
method: Multisite retrospective validation at Johns Hopkins Medicine
500 adult inpatient admissions sampled from 758 eligible cases
Compared iHGR and clinician-selected order sets against physician-adjudicated chart review
evidence_signal: In the abstract, iHGR achieved 81.8% sensitivity and 70.9% specificity versus 61.3%/86.2% for checklist-based order sets and 78.1%/65.4% for clinician-judgement order sets.
watch_item: Performance depended on narrative chart details, and false negatives were linked to missed narrative risk factors, highlighting abstraction and implementation challenges.
paper_title: Multisite Real-World Validation of an Electronic Health Record-Integrated Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool for Venous Thromboembolism Risk Stratification
